items.title: 15th Meeting of ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) Joint Committee held during 6-9 October 2026
items.summary: ASEAN hosted the 15th AITIGA Joint Committee and related meetings to review the progress and negotiations of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) at the ASEAN Secretariat, Jakarta, Indonesia, during 6th to 9th October 2026 along with other sub-committee meetings. The event was conducted in a hybrid format.
key_facts: The meetings provided a valuable forum to deepen collaboration, enhance mutual understanding, and sustain constructive dialogue between both sides.

The Joint Committee (JC) directed all Sub-Committees to expedite pending chapters under the AITIGA Review, establishing firm, time-bound deliverables and urging close coordination to ensure measurable progress.

Both sides underscored their shared commitment to resolve outstanding policy issues, deepen economic integration, and modernize the Agreement into a mutually beneficial framework that strengthens bilateral trade.

items.title: National Medical Library Organises 5th ERMED Consortium National Training-cum-Conference on “Digital Health Resources: Redefining Access Through Libraries
items.summary: The National Medical Library (NML), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, organised the 5th One-Day National Training-cum-Conference on the ERMED Consortium today at the National Medical Library, New Delhi.
items.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
key_facts: She noted that well-equipped libraries and accessible digital resources are essential to strengthening professional competence and enabling healthcare practitioners to provide the best possible care to patients.
She further emphasised that digital health resources are not merely tools for accessing information but also vital enablers of a strong research culture in the country.
Dr. Kotwal underscored the importance of ensuring that digital educational resources are not merely available but are also accessible and useful to medical practitioners, researchers and students.

items.title: Khadi and Village Industries: Weaving the Fabric of an Inclusive and Sustainable India
items.summary: Khadi and Village Industries (KVI) have continued to play a significant role in promoting rural livelihoods, generating employment and strengthening the vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat.
key_facts: Over the years, the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) has supported Khadi institutions through skill development, capacity building and upskilling initiatives.
New product categories such as Khadi denim, designer saris, bridal wear, contemporary shirts and trousers have expanded its appeal among new-age consumers.
An evaluation study conducted by EDII, Ahmedabad, reported that more than 75 per cent of artisans across the schemes experienced a measurable increase in income following the interventions.

items.title: Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal Highlights Need for Rigorous Legal Thinking at CTIL’s 9th Anniversary Celebration
items.summary: Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal, in his video address at the 9th Anniversary Celebration of Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL), held at the Prime Minister’s Museum and Library in New Delhi, on 7 October 2026, said that established rules were being questioned, while emerging issues such as…
key_facts: He underscored the need for a durable international investment law framework that balances investment protection with the regulatory authority of States.
On the occasion, the ninth anniversary issue of the CTIL Magazine, titled “The Emerging Sustainability Landscape: Responding to Shifting Winds”, was released.
The magazine examines the future opportunities and challenges that developing countries may face as they seek to participate in the evolving intersection of trade and sustainability.

items.title: Union Health Ministry Proposes Tighter Curbs on Advertising of Prescription Drugs by Retailers and Wholesalers
items.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to strengthen regulation of advertisements relating to prescription-only medicines.
items.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
key_facts: 861(E), dated 28 September 2026, following consultations with the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB).

Under the existing regulatory framework, pharmaceutical manufacturers are prohibited from advertising drugs covered under Schedule H, Schedule H1 and Schedule X without prior sanction of the Central Government.

The Ministry has invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette containing the draft rules are made available to the public.

items.title: India and Mali commemorate World Cotton Day at United Nations Headquarters in New York
items.summary: The Permanent Missions of India and Mali to the United Nations jointly organized an event on the theme “Cotton for Sustainability: Livelihoods, Value Addition and Partnership” at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on 7 October 2026, commemorating World Cotton Day.
key_facts: He highlighted four priorities: supporting producers’ livelihoods; expanding value addition and access to markets; promoting sustainability; and strengthening technology and partnerships.
He underscored the challenges posed by limited processing capacity, input costs, market access and trade-distorting support.
Outlining Mali’s efforts to expand domestic processing and create employment, he welcomed mutually beneficial partnerships, including South-South cooperation, and acknowledged India as a key partner.

items.title: Union Finance Minister Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman on visit to Singapore for high-level meetings with Singapore Leadership and CEOs of business firms in Singapore
items.summary: Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman is on an official visit to Singapore from 9th to 11th October 2026.
key_facts: During the official visit, FM Smt. Sitharaman will hold a series of high-level engagements with the leadership of Singapore, senior members of the business and investment community, and global institutional investors.
Singapore is India’s largest source of FDI, with cumulative FDI inflows of around USD 194.68 billion during April 2000–March 2026.
Singaporean institutional investors, including GIC and Temasek, have significant investments across the Indian economy.
